difficulty.notes: Degenerate case: the bust param is just (new Date()).getTime() appended inline in the _ajax.call wrapper. No crypto; deterministic but time-varying. The role oracle now includes path diversity: jQuery.extend as a 0.5 generic settings utility, login-side request builders/wrappers and jQuery.ajax as 0.2 path roles, and several off-chain URL/date decoys. There is no legitimate 0.7 nested helper because no separate helper constructs the bust value.

task_contract.anchor_definition: The ajax wrapper (_ajax.call) that appends bust=(new Date()).getTime() to the request URL. The timestamp construction is inline, so the 0.7 nested-helper tier is intentionally empty.

behavior_category.subtype: millisecond timestamp appended as bust query parameter
behavior_category.recompute_check: bust === Date.now() at request time (time-varying; not a fixed expected value)

near_categories.why_not: No local UI/application state is encoded; bust is just the wall-clock time.
Only a cache-buster query param is appended; the request body is unchanged.

evidence: Readable source; the bust generation is a two-line append in one wrapper.

audit.answer_match: Yes: the 1.json case 12 code and oracle.primary_anchor both resolve to _ajax.call in common.js.
audit.question_direction: The visible question asks for the complete function whose own body generates and appends `bust`, which points to _ajax.call.
audit.role_diversity: Added 0.5 and 0.2 path roles plus off-chain decoys. The 0.7 tier is recorded as empty because the target value is generated inline rather than by a nested helper.
